Writing a diary entry

Ficha para imprimir
123456
1

Pregunta de arranquePiensa 30 segundos antes de seguir

¿Has escrito alguna vez un diario? ¿Qué cuenta alguien cuando escribe «Dear Diary, today was the best day ever…»?

Escribe o di en voz alta tu respuesta. Después .

Cuenta lo que le ha pasado ese día, en orden, y sobre todo cómo se ha sentido. Una entrada de diario es un texto personal: se escribe en primera persona (I, we), en pasado (I went, it was) y con fecha. En este tema aprenderás a escribir una paso a paso.

2

Aprende9 bloques cortos

What is a diary?

A diary (or journal) is a notebook where people write about their days: what happened, what they thought and how they felt. Each text is called an entry. Diaries are personal and informal: you write for yourself, so you can be honest and use friendly language.

Some famous books are diaries, real or invented, and many explorers and scientists kept diaries of their trips. En castellano: diary es «diario» y, cuidado, también «agenda». Journal es más bien un cuaderno de notas o reflexiones.

The parts of an entry

A diary entry has a simple structure. 1. Date at the top: «Saturday, 12th November». 2. Greeting (optional): «Dear Diary,». 3. Introduction: one or two sentences to say what the day was like: «Today was a strange day.»

4. Body: the events in order, with details. 5. Feelings: how you felt and why. 6. Ending: a final thought or something about tomorrow: «I can't wait for tomorrow!», «I hope I sleep well tonight.» You can sign with your name or See you tomorrow!

Vídeo: How to write a diary · Teacher Joan (YouTube) · 147 mil visualizaciones

First person and past simple

A diary is written in the first person: I, me, my, we, us, our. «I woke up late and my mum was angry.» «We went to the cinema.»

Most of the text is in the past simple, because we tell what happened today or yesterday: I went, I saw, it was, we played. Remember the regular -ed and the irregular verbs. At the end we can use the future: «Tomorrow I'm going to tell her.» Consejo: repasa la lista de irregulares antes de escribir.

Ordering events: connectors

To tell the events in order, use time connectors: First, Then, Next, After that, Later, In the afternoon, In the evening, Finally, At the end of the day.

To join ideas, use and (y), but (pero), because (porque), so (así que) and when (cuando): «I was nervous because it was my first match.» «It started to rain, so we went home.» «I wanted to go out, but I had homework.» «When I arrived, everybody was singing.»

Talking about feelings

The heart of a diary is feelings. Use adjectives: happy, excited (emocionado), proud (orgulloso), relieved (aliviado), surprised, nervous, worried (preocupado), scared, bored, disappointed (decepcionado), angry, sad, embarrassed (avergonzado).

Say why: «I felt proud because I scored a goal.» «I was disappointed when the trip was cancelled.» Make them stronger with very, really or so: «I was so excited!» Ojo: embarrassed no es «embarazada», sino «avergonzado».

Adding details

A good entry has details that make the reader see the scene. Instead of «I went to the park. It was good», write: «After school I went to the park with Leo. It was sunny and the leaves were orange and yellow. We played tag near the fountain and I fell in a puddle!»

Use the five senses: what did you see, hear, smell, taste, touch? Use adjectives and numbers: «a huge chocolate cake with eleven candles». Add what people said: «My teacher said, "Well done!"».

A model entry

Read Nil's entry: «Wednesday, 9th March. Dear Diary, today was an amazing day! In the morning we had a surprise in class: a real scientist came to talk about volcanoes. First, she showed us some rocks from Lanzarote. Then we made a small volcano with bicarbonate and vinegar. When it erupted, the red foam went everywhere, even on my trainers! Everybody laughed. After that, I asked her a question and she said it was a very good question. I felt really proud. In the afternoon I told my parents about it. Finally, I decided something: I'm going to be a volcanologist! See you tomorrow, Nil.»

Check your text

Before you finish, proofread (revisa) your entry with this checklist. ☐ Date at the top? ☐ First person (I, we)? ☐ Past simple verbs correct (went, not goed)? ☐ Connectors to put events in order? ☐ Feelings and reasons with because?

☐ Capital letters at the start of sentences, for I, names, days and months (Monday, March)? ☐ Full stops and commas? ☐ Details to make it interesting? Read it aloud: if something sounds strange, change it. A good writer always revises.

Let's write: your entry

Now it's your turn. Choose a real day (your birthday, a trip, a match, a day when something went wrong) or an imaginary day (a day as a pirate, a day on Mars). Plan first: write five key events in order and two feelings.

Then write 80-100 words using the structure: date, greeting, introduction, events with connectors, feelings, ending. Finally, check it with the checklist and swap with a partner: they can tell you one thing they liked and one thing to improve. Consejo: escribir un poco cada día en inglés es una forma estupenda de practicar.

Ejemplos resueltos

Ejemplo 1. Join with because: «I was happy. My team won.»

  1. because explica la causa.
  2. Une las dos frases.

Resultado: I was happy because my team won.

Ejemplo 2. Improve: «I went to the beach. It was nice.»

  1. Añade con quién, qué tiempo hizo y qué hiciste.
  2. Usa adjetivos y un sentimiento.

Resultado: I went to the beach with my cousins. It was hot and sunny, and we built a huge sandcastle. I felt so happy!

Ejemplo 3. Correct the entry: «monday, 3rd april. today i goed to the dentist.»

  1. Mayúsculas en días, meses, inicio de frase e I.
  2. go → went.

Resultado: Monday, 3rd April. Today I went to the dentist.

Errores típicos

  • Escribir en presente lo que ya pasó: «Today I go to the zoo» → «Today I went to the zoo».
  • Escribir i en minúscula: en inglés «I» siempre va en mayúscula.
  • Escribir días y meses en minúscula: «monday, march» → «Monday, March».
  • Contar hechos sin decir cómo te sentiste ni por qué.
  • Confundir embarrassed (avergonzado) con «embarazada».

Ejercicios

Hazlos en tu cuaderno y después abre la solución.

  1. Write the date in English: viernes 6 de mayo.

    Ver solución
    Friday, 6th May.

  2. Put in order: Finally / First / Then / After that.

    Ver solución
    First, Then, After that, Finally.

  3. Complete: «I was nervous ___ it was my first exam.»

    Ver solución
    because.

  4. Complete: «It was raining, ___ we stayed at home.»

    Ver solución
    so.

  5. Translate: orgulloso, aliviado, decepcionado.

    Ver solución
    proud, relieved, disappointed.

  6. Change to the past: «I wake up and I have breakfast.»

    Ver solución
    I woke up and I had breakfast.

  7. Add a feeling: «My grandma gave me a puppy.»

    Ver solución
    Model answer: I was so excited because I always wanted a puppy!

  8. Correct: «yesterday me and my friend goes to the park»

    Ver solución
    Yesterday my friend and I went to the park.

  9. Write a good ending for a diary entry.

    Ver solución
    Model answer: I can't wait for tomorrow! / I hope tomorrow is better.

  10. Write a short entry (5 sentences) about today.

    Ver solución
    Model answer: Tuesday, 15th March. Dear Diary, today was busy. First, I had a maths test. Then I played basketball and we won. I felt really proud because I scored six points.

Según cómo respondas, la tarjeta vuelve mañana, en 3, en 7 o en 21 días.

Para familias

  • Regaladle una libreta para escribir dos o tres frases en inglés cada noche durante una semana.
  • Leed juntos su entrada y preguntad por los sentimientos: «How did you feel? Why?».
  • Repasad juntos las tarjetas del paso 6 dos minutos al día durante una semana.

Para profesores

Saberes: Producción de textos escritos personales; la entrada de diario: estructura, pasado simple, conectores y expresión de sentimientos; revisión del texto (Lengua Extranjera) (RD 157/2022, tercer ciclo de Primaria).

  • Diario de clase: cada día un alumno escribe la entrada.
  • Diario de un personaje histórico o de un animal del zoo.
  • Corrección por parejas con la lista de revisión.

Qué vas a aprender

  • Know the parts and features of a diary entry (entrada de diario)
  • Write in the first person and in the past simple
  • Use connectors and time words to order events
  • Express feelings and opinions, and check your text
